CREATION_RULE_CONTEXT.NETWORK_ENVIRONMENT_CONSTRAINTS: Deterministic isolated Linux routing model; no host-route mutation or external infrastructure.

inputs.REQUESTED_DOMAIN: Linux route-table and policy-routing control plane in Go, Ansible-managed fleet rollout, and network operations dashboard

CANDIDATES.ENGINEERING_OBJECTIVE: Build a production-style Go route control plane that models desired route and policy state, reconciles it across a multi-node Linux fleet, detects drift, protects management reachability, records revision history, and exposes the same lifecycle through an operator dashboard and Ansible-driven installation/configuration.
CANDIDATES.SCALE_FIT: VERY_HIGH: naturally supports >3000 substantive LOC, 20-30 coupled manifestations, and 25-30 non-duplicative F2P cases.

CANDIDATES.ENGINEERING_OBJECTIVE: Implement atomic route-table and FIB-rule transactions, dependency ordering, validation, rollback and restart recovery.
Inventory, route snapshots, drift analytics, remediation waves and dashboard workflows across nodes.
CANDIDATES.SCALE_FIT: HIGH but route mutation semantics are less central.

outputs.WHY_THIS_ONE: It keeps Go API route/policy transactions, Ansible fleet deployment, and frontend operations as coupled first-class responsibilities while remaining safely deterministic through an isolated kernel model.
outputs.DUPLICATE_RISK_NOTES: Do not clone edge-router-runtime; this task manages host route/FIB desired state, not HTTP traffic routing.
